item.title: HABITAT SELECTION BY MOOSE IN AN EMERGENT LOW-DENSITY EDGE POPULATION
item.description: The Adirondack Park in northern New York contains about 700 moose (Alces alces) that persist as a low-density population (0.03 moose/km2) that occurs along the periphery of the moose’s southern range in the eastern United States. item.title: WOLF PREDATION ON MOOSE IN NORTH–CENTRAL BRITISH COLUMBIA
item.description: Moose populations declined substantially following widespread salvage logging of mountain pine beetle affected forests in interior British Columbia (B.C.) in the 2000s. The impact of wolf predation on moose was not well-understood in the context of extensive landscape change. item.title: SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL OCCURRENCES OF PRAIRIE MOOSE ACROSS AN URBAN TO RURAL GRADIENT IN SASKATOON, CANADA
item.description: The geographic range and abundance of North American moose (Alces alces) has varied over recent decades, with contractions in areas, recolonization of historical habitats and dispersals into new areas and, notably, increased moose sightings near developed, urban areas. item.description: Changes in moose populations are often evaluated using aerial surveys, which are expensive and dependent upon weather conditions and logistical constraints that sometimes preclude their completion each year. item.title: POPULATION AND HARVEST TRENDS OF MOOSE IN SASKATCHEWAN
item.description: Moose are an integral species of the boreal forest and highly valued by Indigenous peoples and licensed hunters in Saskatchewan. Information from 27 aerial surveys (1998–2022) indicate moose populations are generally declining (range: λ = 0.96 to 1.02) across much of the southern boreal forest and may be stable in the non-forested areas of the province.
